theme: Clinical data and mental health services
significance: This study used routinely collected mental-health records to examine antipsychotic polypharmacy and adverse drug reactions in a large clinical population.
contribution: First author; led the study examining prescribing and adverse outcomes using electronic health record data.

significance: A national school-registry study of more than seven million pupils examining autism incidence and geographic variation across England.
contribution: Joint first author; contributed population and spatial epidemiological analysis within a large interdisciplinary collaboration.

significance: A national study examining how US substance-use treatment providers responded to the opioid epidemic, including geographic and organisational variation in access to opioid agonist treatment.
contribution: First author; led the analysis of national treatment-provider data and interpretation of variation in evidence-based treatment provision.

significance: A population-based study examining demographic, socioeconomic, and health inequalities in unmet need for mental-health treatment in the United States over time.
contribution: First author; led the epidemiological analysis of repeated national survey data on inequalities in access to mental-health treatment.

theme: Addiction, inequality, and access to care
significance: A prospective cohort study examining social deprivation and comorbid mental-health diagnosis as predictors of treatment access among people with opioid use disorder.
contribution: Contributed expertise in psychiatric epidemiology, addiction treatment, inequalities, and quantitative analysis.
